reading.body:
A single OpenStreetMap node tagged as a data center is the entire evidence for iZOOM.it, and nothing in the record confirms the facility exists or operates.

The record is a self-reported map tag, not a verified facility. Its name embeds a ".it" domain, a naming pattern common among Italian web-hosting and domain-registration businesses, which makes a small hosting or IT-services operation plausible. The record's own research note states that no operator website, press coverage, or Italian business registration could be confirmed because search quota ran out, so the entry is filed as plausible rather than established. It sits in northern Italy, 18.7 miles from Parma Airport, with no city or region recorded.

For AI infrastructure, the distinction that matters is scale, and this record carries none. A hyperscale campus and a single rack in a hosting office can both receive the same map tag, and the gap between them is the gap between hundreds of megawatts and a few kilowatts. The capacity field is empty, which means no load figure is recorded, not that the load is zero. Records like this cannot be summed into any power estimate, and treating them as confirmed data centers would inflate counts without adding a single megawatt.

What the data does not say is whether iZOOM.it is or is not a data center. There is no operator, no website, no capacity, no build date, and no confirmation of current operation. The only geographic detail is a coordinate pair and a distance to the nearest airport. The honest reading is that this is an unverified point on a map, and the absence of confirmation is a limit of the research session, not a finding about the business.
